basis: snapshot narrativeCache.data (full read of all five pool deep dives, bridge, sensitivity, scenarios, catalysts, risks, sources and the segment fact gate). report.pdf is well-formed at 50 pages, but pdftotext was unavailable to the grader and no run.log was archived, so page layout is unverified. Scored by the nightly routine; transcribed into the repository by hand because the routine's push was refused.

justifications.depth: All five divisions get full deep dives that reason in the unit of the business rather than summarising it: pulp cash cost of USD 280/t at Paso de los Toros against CMPC's USD 254, EUR 10/MWh of captured power price worth about EUR 40m of EBIT, and the Leuna allocation inverted into roughly EUR 636 of EBITDA per nameplate tonne.
justifications.coverage: Fibres, Energy, Adhesive Materials, Biofuels & Biochemicals and the paper businesses are all valued with their own economics, and the divisions in corporate transition are handled on their announced terms rather than on a generic multiple.
justifications.logic: Each division states what its allocation requires and what would break it, and the group bridge follows those parts instead of a top-down multiple. The chain weakens where the same asset carries different numbers in different sections.
justifications.evidence: Dated, attributed figures throughout, including competitor cash costs, Finnish generation volumes and the segment fact gate's own confidence labels — the same sourcing standard as the strongest Tesla single-writer runs.
justifications.valuation: A parts-based bridge with per-division multiples and a populated sensitivity grid, but the bear case lands only 1.4% below the market price, so the downside scenario carries almost no information.
justifications.readability: Numeric consistency slips in ways a reader will catch: Leuna appears as EUR 756m/758m warranted against EUR 176m/727m allocated within one section, the sensitivity axis is labelled 2027E while carrying the 2026 EBITDA of EUR 1,846m, and three of the seven risk rows name the wrong division.

summary: First single-writer run on a company that is not Tesla, and it lands level with the multi-stage UPM report from 13 August at 4.2 — but by a different route: deeper per-division economics and equally strong sourcing, against weaker numeric hygiene. The pipeline comparison therefore no longer rests on Tesla alone.
issues: Leuna carries two different warranted values and two different allocations inside one section
Sensitivity axis labelled 2027E but populated with 2026 EBITDA (EUR 1,846m)
Bear case only 1.4% below the market price
Three of seven risk rows attributed to the wrong division
No run.log archived, so page layout could not be checked
